prior_opinions.quote: Using an experimental design involving 39 early childhood centers (687 families), we find no effects of the intervention on the outcomes of interest. This finding contrasts with those found in a previous edition of the program in 2018, which showed improvements in parental involvement, in the quality of parent–child interaction, and in adult–child language patterns (Balsa in Child & Youth Care Forum 53:1–22, 2023a; Balsa in Behavioural Public Policy 7: 607–643, 2023c; Bloomfield in Review of the Economics of the Household 21:95–130, 2023).
prior_opinions.reason: The supplied source text is a publisher page containing only the abstract, footnotes, and references without the main Methods, Results, or Discussion sections. The abstract contrasts null effects on unspecified 'outcomes of interest' in the 2020 e-messaging-only COVID-19 intervention (implemented without the 2018 8-session workshop and, per Footnote 8, without observational data) against three papers reporting results from 'a previous edition of the program in 2018': Balsa et al. (2023a, target 0), Balsa et al. (2023c, target 1), and Bloomfield et al. (2022/2023, shipped row 1498, doi: 10.1007/s11150-021-09593-4). Without the full text, the evidence does not settle (1) whether the specific parenting-competence and parent-child interaction outcomes of Balsa et al. (2023a) were empirically retested in the 2020 study rather than cited as contrasting background from the 2018 program, or (2) whether Balsa et al. (2023a) and shipped row 1498 are multiple outcome reports of the same 2018 Crianza Positiva experiment. No prior adjudication file existed.
